2610.13910.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
2610.13910.paper_summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly analyze and reason about images, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations faithfully encode the structured relations required for such reasoning. We introduce EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), a metric for testing whether representations consistently encode concepts under controlled one-concept interventions, and CASP-VL (Causally controlled Spatial Perturbations for Vision-Language models), a benchmark of causally controlled spatial perturbations derived from Visual Genome scene graphs. Across multiple VLM architectures, we find that spatial relations are represented substantially less faithfully than lexical information, even when the same models score well above chance on compositional benchmarks. Further analysis shows that the relation is identifiable at the predicate's own tokens but is lost when the sentence is aggregated into a global representation, whether through the (EOS) token or by mean pooling. These findings reveal a systematic failure invisible to output-based evaluation: VLMs do not preserve, in the representation used downstream, relational information that is present in their own input.
2610.13910.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言模型（VLMs）越來越多地分析和推理圖像，但尚不清楚它們的內部表示是否忠實地編碼了進行此類推理所需的結構關係。<lb/>我們引入了EICS（評估不變概念穩定性），這是一種測試表示是否在受控的單一概念干預下持續編碼概念的度量，還有CASP-VL（因果控制的空間擾動用於視覺-語言模型），這是一個基於Visual Genome場景圖的因果控制空間擾動基準。<lb/>在多個VLM架構中，我們發現空間關係的表示明顯不如詞彙信息的表示忠實，即使相同的模型在組合基準上得分遠高於隨機水平。<lb/>進一步分析顯示，該關係在謂詞的自身標記中是可識別的，但在句子聚合為全局表示時卻會丟失，無論是通過（EOS）標記還是通過均值池化。<lb/>這些發現揭示了一種在基於輸出的評估中看不見的系統性失敗：VLMs在下游使用的表示中不保留其自身輸入中存在的關係信息。
2610.13910.author: Shubh Garg et.al.
